title: Relative dualizing line of an arbitrary nodal family
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume every geometric fibre is nonempty, reduced, pure of dimension one and at worst nodal: at a singular geometric point its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, as in [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The relative dualizing sheaf $\omega_{X/T}$ exists and is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. Here the relative dualizing sheaf means $H^{-1}(f^!\mathcal O_T)$, where $f^!$ is the right adjoint of derived direct image on derived quasi-coherent modules; the relative dualizing complex is canonically $f^!\mathcal O_T\simeq\omega_{X/T}[1]$. For every morphism $a:T'\to T$, with $X'=X\times_TT'$ and $b:X'\to X$, there is a canonical isomorphism $b^*\omega_{X/T}\simeq\omega_{X'/T'}$, compatible with composition of base changes and isomorphisms of families. On the smooth locus it is the module of relative differentials. In particular its restriction to a fibre is that fibre's Serre-duality module. No Noetherian, smooth-generic-fibre, irreducibility, stability or fixed-genus hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0E6R, lemma-gorenstein-dualizing, and the relative dualizing complex discussion immediately preceding it; nodal fibres are Gorenstein. Arbitrary-base nodal specialization of this lemma.

proof.text: Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni s$ an affine open and $U'=\operatorname{Spec}B'\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ an affine open containing $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] $B'$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra, so $S=B'\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ is a finite type $\kappa(s)$-algebra and $\operatorname{Spec}S=U'\cap X_s$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The geometric fibre $X_{\bar s}=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), pure of dimension one, with closed points smooth or nodes; by (1) implies (2) of [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] it has an affine open cover by spectra of local complete intersections over $\overline{\kappa(s)}$. The preimage of $U'$ in $X_{\bar s}$ is the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\overline{\kappa(s)})$ (same two lemmas), so [lem-trf-lci-affine-open-locality] makes $S\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\overline{\kappa(s)}$ a local complete intersection over $\overline{\kappa(s)}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] makes $S$ a local complete intersection over $\kappa(s)$. By [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] its localization $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(s)$. As $f$ is flat and locally finitely presented, [lem-trf-syntomic-pointwise-local-model] gives a chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\ni x$ over $V$, $B=P/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, a relative global complete intersection. Its nonempty fibres have dimension $n-c$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. The fibre over $s$ is a nonempty open of $X_s$, and [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies its local dimensions with those of the pure one-dimensional $X_{\bar s}$; thus $n=c+1$. Only the geometric fibre over $\overline{\kappa(s)}$ is used; no dualizing datum is presumed.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change); morphisms.tex Tags 01TQ, 01UE and 01UG; curves.tex Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci).

proof.text: The equations on each chart are Koszul-regular. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] makes them regular in $P_{\mathfrak q}$ for every prime containing $I=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] makes the localized Koszul complex exact in positive degrees. At a prime not containing $I$, some $h_j$ is a unit: on the wedge basis of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], exterior multiplication by $h_j^{-1}e_j$ is a contraction, since $d(h_j^{-1}e_j\wedge z)+h_j^{-1}e_j\wedge dz=z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], localization commutes with the kernels, images and quotients defining Koszul homology, so its positive homology vanishes at every prime. Such a module is zero: if $0\ne m$, choose a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator; $m/1=0$ there would give $s m=0$ for an $s$ outside that ideal, a contradiction. This proves Koszul regularity globally, without asserting that regularity at one prime spreads over a non-Noetherian ring. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal-free] identifies the classes of the $h_j$ with a basis of $I/I^2$, of rank $c$.

source.place: Tag 07D2 (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-koszul), complete localization argument; algebra.tex Tag 00SV.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] to the proper, flat, finitely presented $f$ and set $K=f^!\mathcal O_T$. On the chart in step 1 it is $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/R})[n]$ as a $B$-complex, with the normalized ordered polynomial-refinement comparisons specified by that node. The hypotheses of the unconditional local assertion of [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] hold by steps 1--2, with $d=1$ and conormal rank $c=n-1$. Its map $\rho_i$ sends the unshifted derived Hom to $i_*D_i[-c]$, respecting the $B$-action, where $D_i=(\bigwedge^c I/I^2)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n i^*\Omega^1_{P/T}$. Shifting by $[n]$ gives $D_i[1]$. Only the arbitrary-base local comparison is used; the theorem's final Noetherian global assertion is not used.

source.place: Tags 0E2X, 0E4P, 0BV2 and 0BQZ; arbitrary-base proper comparison as specified in the cited prerequisite.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], the conormal models $E_i=[I/I^2\to i^*\Omega^1_{P/T}]$ have canonical comparisons $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L_{X/T}|_{U_i}$. Thus $L_{X/T}$ is perfect of amplitude $[-1,0]$. Apply [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]: $D=\det L_{X/T}$ is invertible and the model comparisons give $\alpha_i:D_i\simeq D|_{U_i}$, with transitions $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)$. The normalized Koszul comparison in step 3 states exactly that these are the transitions between the polynomial duality models, shifted by $[1]$. Applying $H^{-1}$ therefore gives compatible local maps $H^{-1}(K)|_{U_i}\simeq D|_{U_i}$. Glue these maps and their inverses by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1). For $q\ne-1$, step 3 gives $H^q(K)|_{U_i}=0$ on every chart; every stalk is zero and [pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks] gives $H^q(K)=0$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] with $r=-1$ to obtain $K\simeq H^{-1}(K)[1]$. Hence $\omega_f:=H^{-1}(K)\simeq D$ is invertible and $K\simeq\omega_f[1]$. The maps glued here are module-sheaf maps, not arbitrary derived maps.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, normalized Koszul comparisons; sheaves.tex Tags 04TN and 00AN; derived.tex Tag 08J5.

proof.text: For $a:T'\to T$ and $b:X'\to X$, flatness makes the square Tor-independent: the affine $R$-module $B$ is flat, so $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'=B\otimes_RR'$. Hence [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] gives $Lb^*L_{X/T}\simeq L_{X'/T'}$, respecting composition and local models. The pullback comparison of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] gives $\beta_a:b^*D_f\simeq D_{f_a}$ with these compatibilities. Properness, flatness and finite presentation persist by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Charts base change: for a chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and an affine open $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq a^{-1}(V)$, the open $b^{-1}(U)\cap f_a^{-1}(V')$ is $U\times_VV'=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change] presents it as $R'[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h'_1,\ldots,h'_c)$, a relative global complete intersection with the same $n=c+1$. These charts cover $X'$. Steps 2--4 use only such charts and properness, flatness and finite presentation, so they apply to $f_a$. Write $\phi_f:\omega_f\simeq D_f$ and define $\gamma_a=\phi_{f_a}^{-1}\beta_a b^*\phi_f$. For successive base changes the intermediate factors $b_2^*(\phi_{f_a}\phi_{f_a}^{-1})$ cancel; the cocycle for $\beta$ gives the cocycle for $\gamma$. Naturality of the intrinsic cotangent complex and determinant gives compatibility with family isomorphisms. On the smooth locus the cotangent statement gives $L\simeq\Omega^1[0]$. The smooth relative dimension there is one by step 1; [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] makes $\Omega^1$ locally free of rank one; the determinant's two-term formula gives $D\simeq\bigwedge^1\Omega^1=\Omega^1$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ, Tor-independent base change; perfect.tex Tag 0FJY, determinant pullback; curves.tex Tag 0C4D.

proof.text:
For any field-valued point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$, steps 2--4 apply to $f_k:X_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by step 5. For every quasi-coherent $F$ on $X_k$, full faithfulness of degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], the shift $K_{f_k}\simeq\omega_{f_k}[1]$ and the right-adjoint property supplied by [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F,\omega_{f_k})=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_k)}(F[1],K_{f_k})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k)}(R\Gamma(X_k,F)[1],k[0]).$$
The module $k$ is injective among $k$-vector spaces: a linear map from a subspace extends by choosing a complementary subspace and setting it to zero there. Apply [new-stage3-derived-homology-injective-bijective] to the last derived Hom. Since $H^0(R\Gamma(F)[1])=H^1(X_k,F)$, it equals $\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(X_k,F),k)$. This is the defining Serre-duality property, natural in $F$, so $\omega_{f_k}$ is the fibre's dualizing module. The isomorphism $b^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f_k}$ from step 5 proves the asserted restriction statement over every residue field, without requiring an algebraically closed field.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q40-863e83257 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item (6 steps), the one new node lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model (byte-identical to 1c08 and 49a6) and the report. I read every cited statement in full. Sources read: moduli-curves 0E6R with the 0E6P/0E6Q relative-Serre-duality display, curves 0C4E, algebra 00SJ and 00SV, and duality 0E2X, lemma-flat-proper-relative-dualizing, 0E4P and 0BV2. No SGA source is cited. The re-route is justified: lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change and seven other nodes now cite the item, so the old datum route would be a cycle (C6). The closure of the fixed proof_deps (about 2900 nodes) does not contain the item. Statement change: def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres, which imports connected fibres, is replaced by def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion and def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series. The statement is no weaker and the report names the change, so I accept it. FIX (E1/E3, one fault appearing in two steps): the statement now gives geometric fibres only over the chosen algebraic closure of kappa(y). (a) Step 1 used (1)=>(2) of lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion, which needs every algebraically closed Omega. I re-proved it with lfp-affine-opens, nodal-curve-lci-criterion on X_sbar, lem-trf-lci-affine-open-locality and lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change (00SJ), giving the lci fibre ring, then the pointwise criterion, the local model and n=c+1. Both added nodes are on live; lem-trf-lci-geometric-chart-descent is not on live, so I did not use it. (b) Step 5 claimed that a geometric fibre of f_a is a geometric fibre of f; that is false unless kappa(y')/kappa(y) is algebraic. I replaced it by base-changing the rgci charts: U x_V V' = Spec(B (x)_R R') by the open-preimage and affine fibre-product lemmas, and lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change (00SS) shows it is again an rgci with the same n=c+1. Steps 2-4 then apply to f_a. Step 6 now refers to steps 2-4. The other steps are correct. Step 2: Koszul regularity holds over an arbitrary base by local regularity at primes containing I, an explicit contraction elsewhere, and localization exactness. Step 3: the unconditional part of the Koszul comparison applies with d=1 and shift [-c][n]=[1]; only cohomology sheaves are used, so no D(B)-level lift is needed. Step 4: the determinant transitions det(lambda_j^-1 lambda_i) match the model transitions, and both nodes use the same normalization (dual of t-a tensor d(t-a) maps to 1). The H^-1 maps glue by glue-sheaves(1), and concentrated-single with r=-1 gives K = omega[1]. Step 5 (otherwise): Tor-independence from flatness, cotangent and determinant base change, the gamma cocycle, and smooth locus det = Omega^1. Step 6: full faithfulness, the adjunction and the injective target k give the Serre-duality module over every field. New node: statement only, all notions cited, true. Over a qcqs base it is 0A9E/0E4P with 0BV2 and the Omega^n normalization. Over an arbitrary base, existence of f^! is the item's own presupposition. Checked cases: n=0, smooth, non-CM, empty base. Not a duplicate: lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality has no polynomial models; the trf polynomial-chart, pair-localization and rigidity nodes are locally Noetherian; the def-trf-polynomial-duality-* nodes are predicates only. It is not a clause of the item.
